model_annotation: The figure presents two line plots comparing the training reward performance of two methods—“Llama-On-Policy” and “Llama-LUFFY”—on Easy and Hard training sets, respectively. In the top plot (“Easy Training Set”), the x-axis represents “Steps” ranging from 0 to approximately 500 with linear spacing and tick marks every 100 steps; the y-axis represents “Training Rewards” from 0.0 to 0.4, also linearly scaled with ticks every 0.1. The blue line with circular markers labeled “Llama-On-Policy-Easy” starts near 0.0, rises steeply to about 0.3 by step 100, then fluctuates slightly before stabilizing near 0.35–0.4. The red line with square markers labeled “Llama-LUFFY-Easy” follows a similar upward trend, starting at 0.0, reaching ~0.3 by step 100, and plateauing near 0.4, with slightly higher peaks and more variability than the blue line. In the bottom plot (“Hard Training Set”), the x-axis again spans 0 to 500 steps with the same tick spacing, while the y-axis ranges from 0.0 to 0.2 with ticks every 0.1. The blue line “Llama-On-Policy-Hard” begins near 0.0, rises slightly to ~0.03 by step 50, then declines to near 0.0 and remains flat for the rest of training. In contrast, the red line “Llama-LUFFY-Hard” starts at 0.0, climbs steadily to ~0.1 by step 150, then continues to rise more gradually to ~0.2 by step 500, exhibiting consistent improvement with minor fluctuations. Both plots include shaded regions around each line, likely representing standard deviation or confidence intervals.
